# A unit spec replaces Neo.main.DomAccess and never restores it, so a later spec's focus() throws

## Context

Found while running the unit tier across several directories for #18764: `selection/GalleryInternalId.spec.mjs` failed in the combined run and passed alone, and the failing arm moved between runs. It is not a flake and not mine — it reproduces on `dev@e197300297`:

```bash
npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/selection/GalleryInternalId.spec.mjs test/playwright/unit/main/DomEvents.spec.mjs --workers=1
```

One arm fails with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getElementById')` at `src/main/DomAccess.mjs:663`, reached through `Gallery.afterSetMounted` → `component/Base.mjs#focus` → `Neo.main.DomAccess.focus`. Each spec passes on its own.

## The Problem

`test/playwright/setup.mjs:162` installs the remote stub every unit spec relies on:

```js
Neo.main.DomAccess ??= { … }
```

`test/playwright/unit/main/DomEvents.spec.mjs:27-31` then deletes it and imports the real main-thread singletons into the same worker:

```js
delete Neo.main.DomAccess;

const {default: DomAccess}    = await import('../../../../src/main/DomAccess.mjs'),
      {default: DeltaUpdates} = await import('../../../../src/main/DeltaUpdates.mjs'),
      {default: DomEvents}    = await import('../../../../src/main/DomEvents.mjs');
```

Each import registers its singleton on the global namespace, so `Neo.main.DomAccess`, `Neo.main.DeltaUpdates` and `Neo.main.DomEvents` now hold real main-thread objects. `afterAll` (`:43-49`) restores `globalThis.document`, `globalThis.window` and the three patched methods — and nothing else. The namespace entries stay.

Two properties turn that into another spec's failure:

1. **A Playwright worker runs many spec files in one process**, so every later spec in that worker inherits the replacement.
2. **`??=` cannot heal it.** A later `setup()` sees a truthy `Neo.main.DomAccess` and leaves the real singleton in place. Its `focus` then calls `document.getElementById` with the `document` this spec deleted.

The victim is whichever spec focuses a component next, which is why the failing arm moves.

## The Architectural Reality

| surface | today |
|---|---|
| `test/playwright/setup.mjs:162` | `Neo.main.DomAccess ??=` — install-once, so a replacement is permanent for the worker |
| `test/playwright/unit/main/DomEvents.spec.mjs:27` | deletes the stub, imports the real singletons, restores neither |
| `src/main/DomAccess.mjs:663` | `document.getElementById(nodeId)` — the throw site, with `document` gone |
| `src/component/Base.mjs#focus` | every component's focus path goes through `Neo.main.DomAccess.focus` |
| `test/playwright/unit/component/CircleAsync.spec.mjs:26` | `delete Neo.main` in `afterEach` — removes the shared stub wholesale, at run time |
| `test/playwright/unit/component/NativeDragZone.spec.mjs:32-33` | `delete Neo.main.addon` / `delete Neo.main.DomEvents` in `afterEach` |

The last two are the same class: a spec disposing of shared namespace state by deleting it rather than restoring what it found.

## The Fix

- **`DomEvents.spec.mjs` restores the namespace it replaced.** Capture `Neo.main.DomAccess` (and the `DeltaUpdates` / `DomEvents` entries, if the imports create them) before the delete, and put the captured values back in `afterAll`, next to the `document` / `window` restore that is already there.
- **Sweep the population** for the delete-as-cleanup pattern and give each the same treatment where a later spec can observe it.
- The paired run above is the witness, and it must go red again when the restore is removed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — the paired run in *Context* passes, and reverting the restore makes it fail again with the same `getElementById` error.
- [ ] **AC-2** — after `DomEvents.spec.mjs` finishes, `Neo.main.DomAccess`, `Neo.main.DeltaUpdates` and `Neo.main.DomEvents` hold what they held before it ran.
- [ ] **AC-3** — `test/playwright/unit/main/DomEvents.spec.mjs` keeps its own coverage: its arms pass unchanged.
- [ ] **AC-4** — every unit spec that deletes a `Neo.main*` / `Neo.worker.*` entry is enumerated, and each either restores what it replaced or carries a line saying why deleting is correct there.
- [ ] **AC-5** — the full unit tier passes locally with the directory set from the report (`grid`, `selection`, `list`, `table`, `plugin`, `menu`, `form`, `main/DomEvents`, `main/addon/GridDragScroll`).

## Out of Scope

The run-level unit-suite nondeterminism of #17796 (closed NOT_PLANNED): that was one arbitrary casualty per CI run with no spec-local cause. This one is a named spec, a named namespace and a deterministic pairing. · Any change to `setup.mjs`'s `??=` install: making it overwrite would paper over a spec that does not clean up.

## Avoided Traps

- **Calling it a flake and re-running.** The pairing is deterministic; only the victim varies.
- **Making the victim defensive.** `Gallery` is not wrong to focus a component; a spec that leaves a broken singleton behind is.

## Related

#17796 (closed NOT_PLANNED — the run-level pattern this is not) · #18764 (the lane that surfaced it) · #18772 (a separate CI-only test defect, menu pointer-rest)

**The same class, from the other side, on the same day:** `test/playwright/unit/apps/colors/ViewportController.spec.mjs` (PR #18774) installs its main-thread stand-ins only where nothing is registered and removes them in `afterAll`, because a plain object left on a `Neo.main` namespace makes the next spec file's `Neo.setupClass` of the real singleton throw a collision (`src/Neo.mjs:881`). That is this ticket's discipline, arrived at independently. A third instance is the retry direction: a spec calling `Neo.setupClass` in `beforeAll` cannot be retried at all, since the retry re-runs it and collides (observed on `unit/data/TreeStoreValueBanding.spec.mjs:194`, broadcast as a defect-note).
